title: TIME/JAMA: ICE Detention Death Rate Reaches 22-Year High; FY2026 Deadliest on Record
excerpt: TIME magazine and a JAMA medical journal study found that the death rate in ICE detention during fiscal year 2026 was the highest in the 22-year period studied — exceeding even the COVID-19 pandemic spike — with 26 deaths reported in just the first seven months of 2026.
content:
In August 2026, TIME magazine published a major investigative piece alongside a peer-reviewed analysis in the Journal of the American Medical Association (JAMA) documenting that the death rate in ICE detention had reached its highest level in 22 years during fiscal year 2026.

  • JAMA authors wrote that the FY2026 death rate "was the highest in the 22-year study period, exceeding even the COVID-19 era spike," and that it took place in a system with "longstanding failures" compounded by Trump administration policies that "rapidly expanded detention to historically high levels, weakened oversight mechanisms, and worsened conditions of confinement."
  • According to U.S. News & World Report, 26 deaths had been reported through the first seven months of 2026 — on pace to exceed 2025's record-breaking total by more than 25%.
  • ICE simultaneously reduced the public information it provided about detainee deaths, and in June 2026 had eliminated the rule requiring reporting of post-release deaths — making the true toll even harder to track.
  • Researchers noted that causes of death were "identifiable and amenable to intervention," describing them as preventable conditions routinely managed in community medicine.

DHS disputed the findings, claiming "there has been NO spike in deaths." The NIPNLG confirmed that as of September 1, 2026, at least 26 people had died in ICE custody during the calendar year, with the pace expected to break the annual record.
source: TIME / U.S. News & World Report / NIPNLG
